dataset.representation: Symptom_1..Symptom_17 slots -> fixed multi-hot symptom columns
dataset.missing_interpretation: Empty symptom slots mean no additional symptom, not missing clinical measurements.

calibration.brier_definition: Multiclass sum of squared errors, averaged across test rows (range 0..2)

explainability.method: Permutation SHAP of deployed calibrated predict_proba; one seeded permutation

urgency.duplicate_weight_policy: Mean of supplied weights for repeated normalized symptom names (fluid_overload has 6 and 4, mean 5)
urgency.label_source: Disease mean symptom severity from TRAINING rows; relative disease-weight terciles, not clinician urgency labels
urgency.rule_context: All listed symptoms are primary; mild severity, <1 day, no medical history. Agreement is not clinical validation.

limitations: Public symptom-disease associations are not independently verified patient records; dataset does not establish clinical diagnostic accuracy.
Only 304 unique patterns remain after deduplication; held-out support is small and results do not establish external generalization.
The least-populated training classes have fewer than five rows: 5-fold stratification is approximate and some validation folds omit rare classes. Calibration uses the supported fold count.
Hyperparameter search and model selection share training CV folds; CV scores are selection estimates, while the held-out test is used only after selection.
Urgency labels are derived relative severity proxies; clinical urgency is not supervised by clinician labels. Red-flag rules always override to High.
Age, duration and reported intensity are absent from the disease dataset and are not disease-model features; rule triage uses the available context.
SHAP is a seeded sampling estimate, includes absent symptoms, and describes model behaviour rather than medical causation.
Calibration can worsen Brier score on this small dataset; report both measured scores. Confidence is a probability within the known dataset classes, not diagnosis certainty.
disclaimer: Not a medical diagnosis. Consult a qualified healthcare professional. Emergency red flags require immediate medical attention.
